decisions.subject: Pipeline for a Vox-style 60s vertical Arabic explainer

options_considered.label: animation (motion graphics, diagram-led explainers, kinetic typography)
options_considered.reason: Vox style for a software topic is diagram, chart and type led — exactly this pipeline's remit, and its manifest recommends flat-motion-graphics playbooks.

options_considered.label: animated-explainer (fully AI-produced from topic)
options_considered.reason: Assumes generated narration plus generated visuals.
options_considered.rejected_because: Its asset path leans on image and video generation; 0 of 32 image and 0 of 36 video providers are configured, and generated imagery would fight the Vox vector vocabulary anyway.

options_considered.label: cinematic (mood-led, footage-first)
options_considered.reason: Built for supplied footage and trailers.
options_considered.rejected_because: No source footage and no mood-led brief; wrong grammar for an explainer.

decisions.reason: The brief is a diagram-and-type explainer with no footage and no generated imagery, which is the animation pipeline's core case.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime

options_considered.label: HyperFrames (HTML/CSS/GSAP → MP4)
options_considered.reason: The selector routes kinetic typography and HTML/GSAP-native motion here, and the registry's motion-graphics guidance points the same way. Arabic shaping and RTL are native browser text layout rather than something to reimplement, and the stepped blur-free Vox cadence is straightforward in CSS/GSAP.

options_considered.label: Remotion (React components → MP4)
options_considered.reason: Available after this session's dependency install. Owns word-level caption burn and the existing chart stack, and matches the user's existing tasmeem project, so patterns transfer.
options_considered.rejected_because: Recommended against, not rejected — the user decides. In atelier mode the existing chart stack is off-limits anyway, which removes Remotion's main advantage here, and React component authoring is more rigid than HTML/CSS for bespoke typographic motion.

options_considered.label: ffmpeg concat only
options_considered.reason: Available.
options_considered.rejected_because: No composition layer; cannot build animated diagrams, charts or type.

decisions.reason: Both runtimes are available, so the HARD RULE requires presenting both and waiting. Agent recommends HyperFrames for native Arabic/RTL text layout and HTML/GSAP-native stepped motion; Remotion is a legitimate pick, especially to reuse tasmeem patterns and word-level caption burn. Not written into production_plan until the user picks.

decisions.subject: Composition authoring mode

options_considered.label: Atelier — hand-authored scenes, one-off theme and motion
options_considered.reason: The guide defaults hero work to atelier, and the request is for a specific recognisable house style. Stock cut-types are frozen looks that reintroduce sameness, which fails the taste profile's own distinctness gate.

options_considered.label: Templated — stock cut.type scenes in the Explainer composition
options_considered.reason: Faster, cheaper, more reliable; right for batch output and drafts.
options_considered.rejected_because: Recommended against: a Vox look assembled from the shared scene catalogue would read as the catalogue, not as Vox. Costs the user the one thing they asked for.

decisions.reason: Agent recommends atelier and says plainly that it costs more tokens and iteration than templated, so the user opts in knowingly.

decisions.subject: Narration TTS provider

options_considered.label: ElevenLabs via the attached MCP connector
options_considered.reason: User's explicit choice at the preflight blocker gate. Best Arabic prosody of the available options and the only one with an auditionable voice library. Currently blocked: the connector returned a permissions error and needs reconnecting.

options_considered.label: ElevenLabs via a direct API key in this container
options_considered.reason: Would activate the in-registry tts_selector path with proper cost tracking.
options_considered.rejected_because: User chose the connector route instead.

options_considered.label: piper_tts, ar_JO-kareem-medium, fully local and free
options_considered.reason: Free, offline, installable now; confirmed Jordanian Arabic voice exists in the piper voice index.
options_considered.rejected_because: Held as the documented fallback, not executed. Audibly synthetic with a fixed accent — a real downgrade, and the no-unilateral-substitutions rule requires approval.

options_considered.label: No narration — caption-led
options_considered.reason: Zero cost, nothing blocked, native to a sound-off feed.
options_considered.rejected_because: User chose a narrated path.

decisions.reason: Explicit user choice at the narration gate. Recorded as blocked rather than silently substituted; the assets stage cannot start until it is reconnected or a fallback is approved.

options_considered.reason: The only configured music capability on this machine, free, and a sparse tense bed is all the design read wants.

options_considered.label: Generated soundtrack (elevenlabs_soundtrack, suno, google and 5 others)

options_considered.rejected_because: 0 of 8 music generation providers configured.

decisions.subject: Style playbook

options_considered.label: Custom generated playbook: vox-ar-explainer
options_considered.reason: No preset encodes the load-bearing choices — square corners, single saturated accent on near-black, stepped blur-free motion, word-level Arabic reveals.

options_considered.label: flat-motion-graphics preset (manifest-recommended)
options_considered.reason: Closest preset and officially recommended for this pipeline.
options_considered.rejected_because: Taste direction forbids letting preset availability override the design read; it carries none of the Arabic text constraints.

options_considered.label: minimalist-diagram preset
options_considered.reason: Diagram-led fit.
options_considered.rejected_because: Too restrained for the Vox stamped read; no accent logic.

decisions.reason: The Arabic constraints and the Vox cadence both need encoding in the playbook itself rather than being remembered per scene.

decisions.subject: Concept direction

options_considered.label: The loop you never see — diagram-led cycle
options_considered.reason: Only concept whose central claim rests on a primary source; closes the clearest research gap; rotation is motion that means something.

options_considered.label: It never read your code — highlighter sweep over a file tree
options_considered.reason: Busts the most load-bearing misconception and is the most recognisably Vox moment available.
options_considered.rejected_because: Runner-up only. Its central claim rests on a secondary source, so it must be phrased as behaviour rather than architecture.

options_considered.label: Felt faster, measured slower — two-bar divergence chart
options_considered.reason: Best single number in the brief, from an RCT, and the canonical Vox chart moment.
options_considered.rejected_because: Runner-up. METR's caveat costs roughly a fifth of a 60-second word budget, and it is the least flattering frame for the subject.

options_considered.label: What it decided while you weren't looking — stacking decision chips
options_considered.reason: Closest to the audience's lived pain, cheapest to build, most Arabic-native.
options_considered.rejected_because: Runner-up. Teaches a caution rather than a mechanism, so the viewer leaves with less.

decisions.reason: Four genuinely different concepts across four animation approaches and four narrative structures. Agent recommends c1; the user may select, mix or redirect.

decisions.subject: Signature device placement across scenes

options_considered.label: Ring appears in sc3 (introduction) and sc7 (hero) only; other scenes carry their own subjects
options_considered.reason: Satisfies the bespoke-composition scarcity rule — the signature device earns weight by being scarce — and gives every scene a distinct primary visual subject.

options_considered.label: Ring present in sc3-sc8, rotating to indicate the current phase
options_considered.reason: Reads as a coherent system and is easier to author.
options_considered.rejected_because: This was my first draft and it is precisely the hero-component spine the skill forbids: one striking visual reused every scene with different text underneath, which is branded slides rather than a film. Caught at self-review and re-planned before writing the artifact.

decisions.reason: The phase is now carried by a small mono eyebrow overlay instead of by the device, freeing sc4/sc5/sc6/sc8 to carry a file tree, a diff, a test bar and a tally grid as their own subjects.

decisions.subject: Caption treatment

options_considered.label: Separate caption sidecar file, nothing burned in
options_considered.reason: On-screen labels name mechanisms the narration never says, so burning a transcript on top would produce the doubled-phrase amateurism the skill warns about. The sidecar still serves sound-off and accessibility.

options_considered.label: Burn word-level Arabic captions into the frame
options_considered.reason: Strong for sound-off feeds.
options_considered.rejected_because: Would collide with the eyebrow label system and double the text load in a vertical frame; also HyperFrames has no word-level caption-burn parity yet.

decisions.reason: Keeps one role per text element. sc10 is the single declared exception where on-screen line and narration line coincide.

decisions.subject: Runtime dependency delivery (GSAP and fonts)

options_considered.label: Vendor GSAP and the Cairo/JetBrains Mono woff2 subsets into the workspace
options_considered.reason: The render browser has no tunnel to jsdelivr or gstatic — validate failed with ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED and the timeline never constructed. Vendoring also makes the render deterministic and offline-safe.

options_considered.label: Load GSAP from jsdelivr and fonts from Google Fonts at render time
options_considered.reason: Standard HyperFrames pattern.
options_considered.rejected_because: Blocked by this environment's network policy inside headless Chrome. Would have rendered an unstyled composition with Arabic falling back to a non-shaping face.

decisions.reason: Fetched server-side where the proxy allows it, then referenced locally. Cairo is declared as a single variable face per subset with font-weight:200 1000 — declaring fixed weights against the same variable file silently flattened 900 to 400.
